name: Tarragon
grown_as: French tarragon, a perennial herb that rarely flowers and sets no seed, so it is grown from cuttings or root division. Russian tarragon (grown from seed) is coarser and flowers. Drawn as French tarragon, with no flower. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A clump 60 to 90 cm high of slender, upright, branching stems, green turning brown and woody at the base, spreading slowly by underground runners. Loose and airy, leaning when tall.

leaf.type: Simple, not lobed (a few lower leaves sometimes split into three at the tip)
leaf.outline: Long and very narrow, like a blade of grass with a midrib, 3 to 8 cm long and 3 to 10 mm wide
leaf.surface: Smooth, without hairs, a little glossy

fruit: None: French tarragon does not set seed.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from cuttings or division.
winter: Dies to the ground; nothing but dead brown stems or bare soil over the roots.

leaf: a long, very narrow leaf with a pointed tip
young: slender upright shoots with narrow leaves set singly, not in pairs
crop: a loose clump of tall slender branched stems
many narrow, smooth, dark green leaves set singly along them
dormant: bare soil or a few dead brown stems, nothing green

look_alikes: Russian tarragon is taller and coarser, paler, and bears loose sprays of tiny yellowish flower heads. Hyssop and rosemary have leaves in opposite pairs. Young toadflax shoots have narrow grey-green leaves but are more crowded and later bear yellow snapdragon flowers.
